Commentary.Commentary: We are back. Ireland players take the field. Followed by Reeza Hendricks and Ryan Rickelton who walk out to open for the Proteas. It will be Matthew Humphreys who will start with the new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, the Proteas need 172 to start their series on a winning note. Can they do it or will the Irish bowlers come hard at them and cause an upset? We shall find out soon. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Neil Rock is for a chat. He acknowledged that there were some runs left out there but felt it was still a good score on the board. The pressure was on, but he went out with confidence, backing himself to get the runs. He noted that one side of the field was shorter while the other made it tricky to find the boundaries. Now, he hopes his team can defend the total.

South Africa did not have the best of starts with the ball but they did well to squeeze the runs through the middle and fag end of the innings. Patrick Kruger was the pick of the bowlers with 4 for 27 in his spell while Mulder, Baartman, Fortuin, and Peter, all played their part and did a decent job to close the innings on a high.

A superb final over from Patrick Kruger has led the South African fightback that has restricted Ireland to 171 for 8 in their 20 overs. Having sent into bat first, Ross Adair got his side off to a flier but could not carry on and both the openers were dismissed in a space of few deliveries. Harry Tector got a start but did not kick on. It was the partnership of Neil Rock (37) and Curtis Campher (49) that got Ireland, back on track. The duo added 59 for the fourth wicket in quick time. George Dockrell made a quick 21 off 16 down the order to take his side past the 170-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Ottneil Baartman serves a length ball, around leg, this one swings down the leg side. It beats the keeper and runs down to fine leg for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Ottneil Baartman to Paul Stirling, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Harry Tector comes out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! The fireworks come to an early end for Ross Adair. He wanted to contiue with his aggressive approach here, but ends up giving away his wicket here. It is a full ball, on off. Ross Adair swings hard at it and ends up hitting it high in the air. The ball travels towards mid on. Tristan Stubbs there moves to his left, settles under it and takes a sharp catch. Wiaan Mulder strikes in his first over.
Commentary.Howout: c Tristan Stubbs b Wiaan Mulder
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Wiaan Mulder to Ross Adair, OUT! c Tristan Stubbs b Wiaan Mulder.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit short this tine, on the pads. Adair tucks it to square leg from inside the crease. This is the first time I am seeing Paul Stirling play the second fiddle up top for Ireland.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Wiaan Mulder to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller one, on the pads, clipped into mid-wicket, but straight to the fielder there.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Wiaan Mulder to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Amazing shot. Mulder pitches it up, full and on middle. Ross Adair dances down the track, gets to the pitch and lofts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Wiaan Mulder to Ross Adair, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short one, shaping away. Adair has a go but gets beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Wiaan Mulder to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Paul Stirling now pushes this full ball into covers for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Wiaan Mulder to Paul Stirling, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Wiaan Mulder.

SIX! BANG! Ross Adair is on fire. Short ball, on off. This one sits up nicely. Ross Adair stays back, swivels and bludgeons it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum. Ireland are 16 for 0 at the end of first.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Too full, sliding down leg. Ross Adair looks to go after it but misses. Wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Ross Adair is a promising prospect for sure. This is some hitting. Pitched up, outside off. Ross Adair stands tall and drills it down the park for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, outside off, shaping away. Adair looks to smack it down the park but gets beaten by the extra bounce this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! CRUNCHED! Ross Adair gets off the mark in remarkable fashion. Back of a length, outside off. Ross Adair backs away and smokes it over the long on for four runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lizaad Williams dishes a short ball, tailing back in. Ross Adair looks to heave it across the line but misses. He gets hit on his rib cage.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lizaad Williams to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ireland and Paul Stirling get off the mark instantly. It is a short ball, on the fourth stump line. Paul Stirling gets on his toes, dabs it towards backward point. One taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lizaad Williams to Paul Stirling, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match proceedings. The South Africa players huddle-up, before spreading out on the field. Followed by Paul Stirling and Ross Adair who walk out to open for Ireland. Lizaad Williams gets the new ball in hand.
Both the teams now walk out and line-up for the National Anthems. It will be South Africa's first, followed by Ireland's.

PITCH REPORT - Vernon Philander is near the deck. He informs that the wicket has a bit of grass covering and it should zip through well. Batters will have a good chance to put in a solid score and the odd ball might do a bit.

Paul Stirling, the captain of Ireland is in for a chat. He expressed his excitement about being in Abu Dhabi and praised the hospitality of the board. He acknowledged the absence of Josh Little but remained optimistic about the team's chances. He highlighted the opportunity for other players to step up and contribute.

Aiden Markram, the captain of South Africa informs that they will bowl first. Informs that it looks like a good wicket with a bit more grass. Adds that he is happy to chase here. Mentions that they are focusing on getting the right result here. Matthew Breetzke gets a start here and adds that they are playing with double spin here.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Ross Adair, Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Neil Rock (WK), George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Fionn Hand. Matthew Humphreys, Craig Young, Ben White.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Ryan Rickelton (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Matthew Breetzke, Aiden Markram (C), Tristan Stubbs, Wiaan Mulder, Patrick Kruger, Bjorn Fortuin, Nqabayomzi Peter, Lizaad Williams, Ottneil Baartman.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of South Africa. They will BOWL first.

Ireland, on the flip side, had a disappointing World Cup and are playing after a couple of months’ break. Paul Stirling is leading a young side with their former skipper Andy Balbirnie being left out and Josh Little taking a break due to CPL commitments. Lorcan Tucker and Harry Tector will lead the batting lineup alongside their skipper Stirling while Mark Adair, Craig Young, and Ben White will be the key figures the bowling lineup. Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, and Gavin Hoey will provide the balance to the squad. With plenty of new faces eager to make a mark at the international level, the series promises to be an enthralling one. So, who are you backing to come out on top? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for the toss and team news coming up shortly!

South Africa are coming off an ODI series loss against Afghanistan. The Proteas will want to put that behind them and start afresh in the shortest format. Aiden Markram continues to lead the T20 side with Reeza Hendricks, Tristan Stubbs, and Ryan Rickelton being the key batters in the squad. Ottniel Baartman, Bjorn Fortuin, and Lungi Ngidi will spearhead the bowling while Wiaan Mulder and Patrick Kruger will provide the all-round strength. South Africa will hope to start the series on a positive note and get a win.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the two-match T20I series between Ireland and South Africa from the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi. The T20 World Cup runners-up, South Africa, will want to give some young-guns a chance to build for the future while Ireland will want to show their mettle and cause an upset.

The stage is set for a thrilling T20I showdown between Ireland and South Africa at Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Zayed Stadium. Fresh from their ICC T20 World Cup runner-up finish, South Africa seeks redemption after a disappointing ODI series loss to Afghanistan. Aiden Markram leads a dynamic Proteas squad that blends experience and youth. Their batting lineup boasts Aiden Markram, Tristan Stubbs, Ryan Rickelton, Reeza Hendricks, and Matthew Breetzke, while the bowling attack features lethal pacers Ottneil Baartman, Lungi Ngidi, Nandre Burger, and Lizaad Williams, complemented by spinners Bjorn Fortuin and Nqabayomzi Peter. Ireland, on the other hand, captained by Paul Stirling, aims to pull off an upset. Their lineup comprises of a talented pool of players. Curtis Campher, Harry Tector, George Dockrell, and the rest would put in a perfect challenge to the Proteas but they will have to play some outstanding cricket to even put up a fight against the mighty Proteas. Can South Africa rebound from their recent setback, or will Ireland script a stunning upset? We shall find out soon.
